doc_name: List of The Cosby Show characters
text: The Cosby Show is an American television sitcom starring Bill Cosby that aired for eight seasons on NBC from 1984 to 1992, focusing on the Huxtable family, an upper middle-class African-American family living in Brooklyn, New York. Dr. Heathcliff "Cliff" Huxtable, who lives in Brooklyn Heights, New York, is known for his comical antics, playful admonishments, and relentless teasing humor. He had a brother, James Theodore Huxtable, who died of rheumatic fever at age 7. In his high school and college years, he was an athlete who competed in wrestling, American football, and track and field. He later served in the Navy before attending medical school and became an obstetrics and gynecology doctor who runs a practice from an office annexed to his home. Most characters outside the family and friends refer to him as "Dr. Huxtable," and he is well-respected in the community. Cliff is married to Clair Huxtable, both of whom attended the fictional Hillman College. Together, they have five children: Sondra, Denise, Theodore (Theo), Vanessa, and Rudith (Rudy). Cliff enjoys live jazz, has an extensive collection of albums, and tries to eat junk food whenever he can get away with it. He is eccentric and silly to most people, especially his family, but is kind-hearted and a dedicated father with a strong sense of humor. A running gag is his repeated attempts to get the grown children to leave the house. Cliff is very playful and enjoys competition, often making bets with Clair over things like the release date of a jazz song or a "Smooth Contest" judged by the children, and he plays a monthly game of pinochle against his father and friends, which sometimes becomes very passionate. He often loses these bets and games, such as never beating his father-in-law at chess, but eventually broke his losing streak at pinochle with the help of Dr. Foster, an expert player and their literary professor at Hillman College. In the pilot episode, Cosby's character is named Clifford, as shown on a house sign, but his full name was later changed to Heathcliff, even though Clair once called him "Heathclifford," and he is commonly known as "Cliff." Originally, Cliff was to be a chauffeur, with humor derived from customer interactions, but the show was changed to feature him as a doctor, with humor coming from his family interactions. Cliff appears in three episodes of A Different World: the pilot (with Rudy), "Rudy and the Snow Queen" (also with Rudy), and "If Chosen, I May Not Run." He is the only character to appear in every episode. Clair Olivia Huxtable (née Hanks) is the elegant, tough, eloquent, and engaging wife of Cliff, known for her relaxed confidence and sharp emphasis. She is intelligent, classy, and successful as a businessperson and a lawyer, rarely losing an argument, and skilled in recalling facts and dates, as shown when she quotes a book passage and page number during a television roundtable. She speaks Spanish and once speaks Portuguese to Theo's teacher. Despite her strictness, she is a loving mother and wife, with her catchphrase "Let the record show." Her character is loosely based on Bill Cosby's wife, Camille Cosby, and her maiden name is the same as Camille's. Her age is directly stated only once, and two episodes provide conflicting information: in season three, Cliff celebrates his 50th birthday, and in season five, Clair celebrates her 46th, indicating she is six years younger, but in the season four episode "The Locker Room," it is stated she is four years younger. Originally, she was supposed to be a housewife, but when the show aired, she became a lawyer and eventually became a partner in her law firm, helping her family with legal issues and successfully representing her daughter Sondra in a case over dishonest car repairs. She was the chief disciplinarian of the children, as shown when she delivers a scathing speech to Vanessa after she sneaks off to Baltimore to see a rock concert. Clair appears in four episodes of A Different World: "Clair's Last Stand," "Risky Business" (with Theo and Vanessa), "Forever Hold Your Peace" (with Martin and Olivia), and "Success, Lies and Videotapes." She has been ranked highly in several lists of the top television mothers, including being voted "Favorite TV Mom" in 2004 by the Opinion Research Company, included in Film.com's Top 5 Classic TV Moms in 2009, selected in iVillage's "Mommy Dearest: The TV Moms You Love" in May 2012, and named the ninth Most Memorable Female TV Character by AOL in 2012. Sondra Tibideaux (née Huxtable), the eldest daughter, did not appear in the pilot episode, as Clair says, "Why do we have four children?" and Cliff replies, "Because we did not want five." In her first appearance, she is a sophomore in college and 20 years old. She earned a degree from Princeton University and intended to become a lawyer like her mother. She married Elvin Tibideaux in season four and later gave birth to twins named after Nelson and Winnie Mandela. She is serious, responsible, and intelligent, fitting the characteristics of a first-born, though she occasionally has bizarre thoughts (e.g., dropping out of law school to open a wilderness store with Elvin), which she usually recovers from quickly. She is proud of her parents but held to a higher standard than her siblings. Sondra was created when Bill Cosby wanted to show the success of raising a child, and Whitney Houston was considered for the role. Sabrina LeBeauf almost missed out because she is only 10 years younger than Phylicia Rashad. The character is loosely based on Cosby's eldest daughter, Erika. Denise Kendall (née Huxtable) is the second daughter. At the start of the series, she is 16 years old, loves fashion and music, and does not want to attend school to pursue these interests. She is independent, learns lessons on her own, and after a two-year stint at Hillman College, goes to Africa as a photographer's assistant, where she meets and marries Navy Lt. Martin Kendall and becomes stepmother to his three-year-old daughter Olivia. She eventually decides to become a special education teacher and plans to attend Medgar Evers College, but leaves New York when Martin is posted to Singapore. In the series finale, she is revealed to be pregnant. In the first two seasons, she is a popular high schooler with many friends and a changing love life, often mocked by Cliff for her hairstyles and clothing. In later seasons, she becomes more flighty and expresses ideas that confuse Cliff and Clair. In season three, she leaves home to attend Hillman College, a fictional historically Black college where her mother, father, and grandfather were alumni. A spin-off series, A Different World, initially focused on Denise at college, but she was written out after the first season when Lisa Bonet became pregnant. In season five, she travels to Africa, falls in love with and marries Martin, and returns home in the season six premiere, shocking her parents with the news. Cliff and Clair accept the couple when they meet Olivia, who wins their hearts and is welcomed into the family. She appears regularly in the first three seasons, in four episodes each of seasons four and five (a picture of her appears in the opening credits of season four), regularly in season six, and in only a few episodes in season seven. The character is loosely based on Cosby's daughter Erinn, who was about the same age as Denise, and Denise attended Hillman College, modeled after Spelman College. Theodore Aloysius "Theo" Huxtable is the middle child and only son, athletic and obsessed with impressing girls and obtaining a sports car or motorcycle. He is 14 years old at the start of the series. In the pilot, he is lectured by his father for not applying himself at school. In early seasons, he is a troublemaker, such as letting his best friend's younger sister pierce his ear, leading to an infected earlobe, though his behavior improves by the time he leaves high school. A recurring theme in early seasons is his academic struggles, especially in sophomore-year geometry taught by Mrs. Westlake. As the series progresses, he evolves into a successful high school and college student, and in interviews, Cosby noted a similar change in his real-life son, Ennis. While at NYU, it is revealed he has dyslexia, a learning disability that motivates him to work harder and overcome it. By the final season, he becomes a volunteer student teacher helping children with dyslexia at a community center. He is offered a job in San Francisco but turns it down to attend graduate school and continue his volunteer work. In the final episode, he graduates from NYU with a degree in psychology. In the pilot and once in season one ("Bad Dreams"), Vanessa refers to him as "Teddy" instead of "Theo." He has a long-running, on-and-off relationship with Justine, mentioned many times but appearing in only nine episodes. During high school, his best friend is Walter Bradley (Carl Anthony Payne II), known as "Cockroach," who is a scholastic underachiever, though he presents convincing facts in a mock trial that closes the case. The two occasionally compose rap songs for school assignments. When Theo gets tickets to "Dance Mania," only one can enter, and he lets Cockroach have the spot, which makes him uncomfortable when he sees Cockroach on TV and at school the next day. This episode marks Cockroach's final appearance, and he is rarely mentioned afterward. Theo appears in two episodes of A Different World: "My Dinner With Theo" (with Rudy) and "Risky Business" (with Clair and Vanessa). Vanessa Huxtable is the fourth child and third daughter, 11 years old at the start of season one. As she grows, she faces typical teenage issues, such as wearing makeup before her 15th birthday and spending time on the phone with friends. Unlike her brother, she is an excellent student and enjoys school; by the start of season seven, she goes to college one year early. In the final season, she becomes engaged to Dabnis Brickey, a man in his late twenties, who is the head of maintenance at Lincoln University in Pennsylvania, where she enrolls. However, she realizes she is not ready to marry and breaks off the engagement, maintaining they are "just friends" by the end. In early seasons, she is nosy, often sneaking to find out what goes on in the house, especially involving Theo. In a later episode, the tables are turned when Theo catches her friends smoking in her room, though she herself did not participate. She often fights with her younger sister, Rudy, over childish issues, and at one point, their fighting causes damage to their bedrooms and the kitchen ceiling, leading Cliff to declare their rooms off-limits and exile them to the basement until repairs are done. On one occasion, she gets into a physical fight with Denise over a sweater she stole from Denise's closet. During seasons five and six, she has a rebellious phase, engaging in shady activities such as creating a suggestive dance for a music video, sneaking out with a boyfriend after breaking curfew, playing a drinking game with friends, attempting to sneak to a college party, and most famously, sneaking out to a concert in Baltimore with her friends, where everything goes wrong, greatly upsetting Clair. One of her best friends is Kara (Elizabeth Narvaez), who rambles at high speed; when Cliff refers to her as "Turbo Tongue," he usually replies with a bewildered "Thank you." Vanessa appears sporadically in the final two seasons due to being away at college. The character is loosely based on Cosby's daughter Ensa, who was about the same age as Vanessa. Vanessa also appears in the A Different World episode "Risky Business" (with Clair and Theo). Rudith Lillian "Rudy" Huxtable is the youngest child, only five years old at the start of the series. Several of her friends appear throughout the series, including the quiet Peter Chiara, who repeatedly runs out the front door when frightened, and the chauvinist, blues-loving Kenny, whom she nicknames "Bud," who always gets advice from his unseen older brother, leading to misunderstandings and trouble, though he seems to grow out of it. Keshia Knight Pulliam was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award in season two, becoming the youngest nominee ever; one of her fellow nominees was Lisa Bonet, neither of whom won, as they lost to Rhea Perlman from Cheers. The Huxtable family was originally going to have two boys and two girls, but the youngest child, Rudy, was initially supposed to be a boy, and the character was rewritten for a girl (Keshia Knight Pulliam) due to a lack of boys auditioning. Jaleel White, later known for his role as Steve Urkel on Family Matters, revealed in a 2011 interview with Vanity Fair that he auditioned for the role of Rudy. The character is loosely based on Cosby's youngest daughter, Evin, who was about the same age as Rudy. Rudy also appears in three episodes of A Different World: the pilot (with Cliff), "Rudy and the Snow Queen" (also with Cliff), and "My Dinner with Theo" (with Theo). Elvin Tibideaux is Sondra's boyfriend and later husband. They met at Princeton University, where they both earned degrees. They constantly bicker in early episodes, until their interactions with the Huxtables, especially Clair, challenge him to confront his "male-chauvinist" attitudes. After their honeymoon, they shock Cliff and Clair by announcing their intention to forego medical school and law school and start a wilderness supply store in Brooklyn.

doc_name: List of The Cosby Show characters
text: The show features three boys and two girls. The youngest child, Rudy, was originally intended to be a boy, but the character was rewritten as a girl, Keshia Knight Pulliam, due to a lack of boys auditioning. Jaleel White, known for his role as Steve Urkel on Family Matters, revealed in a 2011 interview with Vanity Fair that he had auditioned for the role of Rudy. The character is loosely based on Bill Cosby's youngest daughter, Evin, who was approximately the same age as Rudy. Rudy appears in three episodes of A Different World: the pilot (with Cliff), "Rudy and the Snow Queen" (also with Cliff), and "My Dinner with Theo" (with Theo). Elvin Tibideaux is Sondra's boyfriend and later husband; they met at Princeton University, where they both earned degrees. The two frequently bicker during early episodes until Elvin's interactions with the Huxtables, especially Clair, challenge him to confront his "male-chauvinist" attitudes. After returning from their honeymoon, they shock Cliff and Clair by announcing they will forgo medical school and law school to start a wilderness supply store in Brooklyn. When their children are born, Elvin re-applies to medical school, a decision that convinces Sondra to resume her law school studies. Elvin was a high school wrestler and competed for one year at Princeton University before quitting due to a hip injury. During season three, he helps Theo with strategy and moves. Lt. Martin Kendall is a United States Navy officer, husband of Denise Huxtable, and father of Olivia. He is introduced to the Huxtables after Denise unexpectedly marries him in Africa, unbeknownst to the family. When the newlyweds return, they learn Denise's family does not know about their marriage or him at all, causing initial discomfort for Clair and Cliff, who eventually become accustomed to the blended family. Kendall had an ex-wife, Paula (played by Victoria Rowell), and in the finale, it is revealed that he and Denise are expecting a baby together. Joseph C. Phillips played Sondra's date in a season two episode, a different character than Martin. Martin appears frequently in the sixth season but is only seen in a few episodes of the seventh season, Phillips's final season as a regular, and makes his final appearance in the season eight episode "Olivia Comes Out of the Closet." Martin also appears in the Different World episode "Forever Hold Your Peace" (with Clair and Olivia). Olivia Kendall is Denise Huxtable's precocious stepdaughter, who is three years old when she first appears. Olivia is the only child of Martin and Paula Kendall. After a few years of marriage, her parents divorced, and Paula gave Martin full custody, as she felt overwhelmed by marriage and motherhood. Olivia was raised by her grandparents and father. When Olivia is almost four, Martin marries Denise Huxtable, whom he met in Africa. The new family moves in with Denise's parents, Clair and Cliff Huxtable, who become Olivia's step-grandparents. As a Naval officer, Martin travels frequently, so Olivia spends time with Denise during his absences. Olivia continues to live with her step-grandparents while her parents are in Singapore during the final season. The character Olivia was named after Bill Cosby's wife, Camille Olivia Hanks-Cosby. Raven originally auditioned for the Bill Cosby movie Ghost Dad but did not get the part because she was too young; however, Cosby liked her so much that he created the role of Olivia, his step-granddaughter, for her in the final three seasons. Olivia also appears in the Different World episode "Forever Hold Your Peace" (with Clair and Martin). Pam Tucker is the daughter of Clair Huxtable's first cousin, making her and Clair first cousins once removed. The daughter of a single mother, Pam moves in with the Huxtables after her mother relocates to California to care for Pam's grandmother. Upon moving in, Pam is a high school junior—younger than Vanessa but older than Rudy. At first, she is not used to the Huxtables' upper-middle-class lifestyle or close-knit family dynamics, but eventually fits in and becomes part of the Huxtable family. Pam makes her first appearance in the fourth episode, "A Period of Adjustment," in season seven. Frequently, Pam is shown interacting with her best friend, Charmaine Brown (Karen Malina White), and Charmaine's boyfriend, Lance Rodman (Allen Payne). The character had a mixed reception.
